title: Rochdale’s Breaking Barriers secures core funding to expand its cultural work across Greater Manchester
excerpt: Rochdale-based production company Breaking Barriers has secured three years of GMCA core funding to expand cultural programmes, paid opportunities and creative development across Greater Manchester.
body:
Rochdale-based multidisciplinary production company Breaking Barriers has secured three years of core funding from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to strengthen the organisation and expand its cultural programmes across the region.

Over the funding period, Breaking Barriers plans to offer 42 paid placements through its Young Company programme, giving creatives aged 18–25 hands-on experience working on professional arts productions.

It will also provide 328 paid freelance roles and 45 in-kind artist residencies at its Rochdale base at Richard Street Studios.

Young Company participants will gain practical skills in producing, sound design, filmmaking and direction, with a focus on young people from underrepresented backgrounds who have had fewer opportunities to get into the arts.

A producer development programme will also support 36 creative producers a year to develop their own projects, secure resources and build sustainable careers.

Awarded through the Spirit strand of the GMCA Culture Fund, the investment will support Breaking Barriers to continue delivering theatre, film and immersive outdoor artworks, alongside training, mentoring and paid opportunities for emerging creatives.

Parvez Qadir, Artistic Director of Breaking Barriers, said: “Three years of core funding gives us the stability to plan ahead and grow as a company here in Rochdale. There’s so much creative talent locally, and we can now give more young people paid opportunities to work alongside experienced artists on our productions. It also enables us to keep building partnerships across Greater Manchester and develop projects shaped by local people, bringing their stories to life.”

Bev Craig, Mayor of Greater Manchester, said: “Culture has the power to connect communities, inspire creativity and strengthen pride in the places we call home.

“Through the Greater Manchester Culture Fund, we're investing in a diverse range of cultural organisations that help make our city region such a vibrant and inclusive place to live. Breaking Barriers is a fantastic example of a local company creating opportunities for young people to share their stories, develop their creativity and shape cultural experiences on their doorstep.”

Projects are currently planned to span the boroughs of Rochdale, Bury, Salford, Stockport, Manchester, Tameside and Bolton over three years.

Residents and local communities will help create outdoor artworks using sound, projection and light, alongside films and digital storytelling projects reflecting local experiences.

The funding will also help sustain and expand Breaking Barriers’ theatre in education work.

This includes multi-partnership delivery of Crossing the Line, a theatre and workshop programme tackling child criminal exploitation, which has already reached more than 15,000 young people across more than 220 schools.

Blind Side, exploring violence against women and girls, consent and healthy relationships, will continue to tour. Support from the Spirit strand will enable more time and resources to further expand its reach into other boroughs.

Source: Breaking Barriers.
